issues.title: Session without context manager usage
issues.description: The rule requires all database sessions to use 'with Session(db.engine, expire_on_commit=False) as session:' pattern for proper resource management, but the code creates a session without a context manager and never closes it
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
session = Session(db.engine)
row = session.scalar(stmt)
if not row:
    raise ConversationVariableNotFoundError("conversation variable not found in the database")
row.data = variable.model_dump_json()
session.commit()
issues.rule_name: SQLAlchemy Sessions Must Use Context Managers

issues.title: Database transaction commits called on every variable update instead of batched
issues.description: The ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer now calls flush() inside the loop for each updated conversation variable, rather than batching all updates and flushing once after the loop completes. This causes multiple unnecessary database commits when multiple conversation variables are updated in a single node execution, significantly degrading performance and creating database contention. The original implementation correctly tracked whether any updates occurred with the `updated_any` flag and only flushed once after all updates were queued.

issues.title: Conversation variable persistence layer registered before persistence layer causing event ordering issue
issues.description: The conversation_variable_layer is now registered before the persistence_layer in the graph engine layer stack. In event-driven architectures with layered middleware, the order of layer registration determines the order in which layers receive and process events. By registering conversation_variable_layer first, it will receive and process NodeRunSucceededEvent events before the persistence_layer has a chance to persist the node execution state. This creates a race condition where conversation variables might be updated in the database before the corresponding node execution is persisted, leading to data inconsistency if failures occur between the two operations.

issues.title: Conversation variable persistence failures are silently ignored
issues.description: The ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer calls update() without catching exceptions, relying on the graph engine's blanket exception handler which logs but continues execution. When persistence fails (e.g., database errors, ConversationVariableNotFoundError), the exception is caught by the engine's try-except in event_manager.py, logged, and execution continues. This creates silent data loss where the in-memory variable pool contains updated values but the database doesn't, causing data inconsistency. In the original implementation, these errors would fail the node execution and stop the workflow, providing clear feedback to users.

issues.title: ConversationVariable query missing tenant_id filter
issues.description: The SELECT against the tenant-scoped ConversationVariable table is filtered by id and conversation_id only, with no tenant_id predicate. This violates the requirement that tenant-scoped queries must include tenant_id scoping to prevent cross-tenant data access.
issues.rule_name: Database Queries Must Include tenant_id Scoping

issues.title: Missing return type annotation on __init__
issues.description: The __init__ method is missing an explicit return type annotation (e.g., "-> None"), which violates the requirement that all Python function definitions include type annotations for parameters and return values.
issues.problematic_code_snippet: def __init__(self, variables: dict[tuple[str, str], object] | None = None):
issues.rule_name: Python Functions Must Include Type Annotations

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #30531 - feat: Add conversation variable persistence layer
pr.author: unknown

structured_output.summary:
This PR moves conversation-variable persistence out of the two Variable Assigner nodes (v1 and v2) and into a new graph-engine layer, `ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer`. The layer listens for `NodeRunSucceededEvent`s from `VARIABLE_ASSIGNER` nodes, reads the updated conversation variables from `process_data`, and writes them through a `ConversationVariableUpdater`. The updater implementation moves from `core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/common/impl.py` to `services/conversation_variable_updater.py`, and the layer is attached only in `AdvancedChatAppRunner`. The layering motivation is sound: nodes become side-effect free, and the `ignore_imports` exception for `ext_database` can be dropped.

The refactor changes failure semantics in ways the tests do not cover. Persistence errors used to fail the node. Now they are logged and swallowed by the event manager. A missing `conversation_id` used to raise in both nodes; it now silently skips the write. Single-step debug runs no longer persist anything, because `WorkflowEntry.single_step_run` builds its own engine without this layer. The new updater also leaks a SQLAlchemy session on every call. I'd want these addressed before merging.
structured_output.verdictRationale: Three correctness regressions and one resource leak. (1) Persistence failures are now swallowed: `_notify_layers` catches and logs layer exceptions, so a failed DB write leaves the node reporting SUCCEEDED with a stale row. (2) A missing conversation_id now silently skips the write where it previously raised. (3) Single-step debug runs of assigner nodes no longer update `ConversationVariable` at all, since only the advanced-chat runner registers the layer. (4) The updater opens a Session per update and never closes it. The design direction is good, but these need fixing or an explicit decision before merge.

architecture.overview:
Before this PR, `v1.VariableAssignerNode` and `v2.VariableAssignerNode` called `ConversationVariableUpdater` (implemented in `core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/common/impl.py`) inside `_run()`. The write happened synchronously while the node executed, and a failure failed the node. The graph engine dispatches node-success events to registered `GraphEngineLayer`s through `EventManager._notify_layers`, which catches and logs layer exceptions.

This PR relocates the write. Nodes now only update the in-memory variable pool and emit `process_data`. A new `ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer` subscribes to `NodeRunSucceededEvent`s for `VARIABLE_ASSIGNER` nodes, reads the updated selectors from `process_data`, looks up the current values in the read-only pool, and calls the updater. The updater now lives in `services/conversation_variable_updater.py` and is wired in only by `AdvancedChatAppRunner`. The single-step and draft-run path (`WorkflowEntry.single_step_run`) builds its own `GraphEngine` with only debug, limits, and observability layers, so it no longer persists conversation variables.
steps: Entry point: `AdvancedChatAppRunner` builds the `GraphEngine` via `WorkflowEntry` and attaches layers. This PR adds `ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer(conversation_variable_updater_factory())` at `api/core/app/apps/advanced_chat/app_runner.py` lines 204-205.

Node side: `v1` and `v2` `VariableAssignerNode._run()` no longer touch the database. They write to the variable pool and record `updated_variables` in `process_data` (`api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v1/node.py`, `v2/node.py`).

Event side: when a `NodeRunSucceededEvent` arrives, `api/core/app/layers/conversation_variable_persist_layer.py` filters for `VARIABLE_ASSIGNER`, extracts the selectors, keeps only `CONVERSATION_VARIABLE_NODE_ID` selectors, and calls `update()` then `flush()` on the injected updater.

Persistence: `api/services/conversation_variable_updater.py` selects the `ConversationVariable` row by id and conversation, then writes `variable.model_dump_json()` to `data`. This is the only write path for the advanced-chat runner, and the conversation service reuses it.

Not covered by this wiring: `WorkflowEntry.single_step_run` (`api/core/workflow/workflow_entry.py` ~L77-104) attaches only debug, limits, and observability layers. Single-step assigner runs therefore no longer write to `ConversationVariable`. Failure handling also changes: layer exceptions are caught by `EventManager._notify_layers` and logged, so a failed write no longer fails the node.

findings.title: Persistence failures no longer fail the node
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/app/layers/conversation_variable_persist_layer.py`, `on_event` calls `update()` and `flush()` on the injected updater. `EventManager._notify_layers` catches and logs any exception from a layer, so a failed DB write leaves the node marked SUCCEEDED with stale data. Decide how persistence failures should surface. Either re-raise a dedicated error that fails the run, or persist synchronously in the node and keep the current design only for cases where skipping is acceptable. If the swallowing is kept, document it and add a test asserting that an updater exception is logged and does not propagate. Follow the existing error-propagation style in `api/core/workflow/graph_engine/event_management/event_manager.py`.

findings.title: Missing conversation_id now silently skips persistence
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/app/layers/conversation_variable_persist_layer.py` (~lines 34-36), `on_event` returns silently when `conversation_id` is None. Before this PR, the v1 node raised `VariableOperatorNodeError` and the v2 node raised `ConversationIDNotFoundError` (except in DEBUGGER invocations). Restore that guard, or at minimum log a warning when a conversation variable is assigned without a conversation id. Keep the DEBUGGER exemption if it is still needed. Add a unit test for this branch, which currently has no coverage.

findings.title: Single-step assigner runs no longer persist conversation variables
findings.fixPrompt: Single-step runs of Variable Assigner nodes (`WorkflowEntry.single_step_run` in `api/core/workflow/workflow_entry.py`, called from `api/services/workflow_service.py` around line 696) no longer persist conversation variables, because `ConversationVariablePersistenceLayer` is attached only in `api/core/app/apps/advanced_chat/app_runner.py` (lines 204-205). Decide whether the persistence should also run for single-step and draft runs, which have a conversation id from `get_or_create_conversation`. If yes, attach the same layer in `single_step_run`. Keep layer order and the existing debug/limits/observability layers unchanged. Add a test that a single-step assigner run updates the `ConversationVariable` row.

findings.title: Session leaked on every conversation variable update
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/services/conversation_variable_updater.py`, `ConversationVariableUpdaterImpl.update` (around lines 18-23) creates `session = Session(db.engine)` without closing it. Restore the context-managed form used before this PR, for example `with Session(db.engine) as session, session.begin():` (or `with Session(db.engine) as session:` with an explicit commit). Make sure the `ConversationVariableNotFoundError` raise happens inside the `with` block so the session is closed on that path too.

findings.title: New layer tests do not cover the failure branches or the real updater
findings.body:
The layer tests use `Mock()` for the updater and cover three cases: happy path, non-assigner nodes, and non-conversation selectors. Several branches have no test:

- `conversation_id` is None. This is the regression in the finding above.
- The variable is missing from the pool, so the `isinstance(variable, Variable)` branch runs.
- The updater raises. The swallowing behaviour is untested.
- Selector length under 2.

The node tests also dropped their DB assertions, replacing them with `process_data` checks. Nothing now verifies that `ConversationVariableUpdaterImpl` writes the row or that `AdvancedChatAppRunner` wires the layer. Also, `test_skips_when_outputs_missing` actually sets `process_data` to empty, so its name does not match its body.

::diff{file="api/tests/unit_tests/core/app/layers/test_conversation_variable_persist_layer.py" lines="1-14"}
findings.fixPrompt: Strengthen the tests in `api/tests/unit_tests/core/app/layers/test_conversation_variable_persist_layer.py`. Add cases for: `conversation_id` None (should not silently skip if you adopt that fix), a conversation selector missing from the pool, and an updater that raises (assert the behaviour you choose). Rename `test_skips_when_outputs_missing` to match what it asserts, since it uses empty `process_data`. Add one test that uses the real `ConversationVariableUpdaterImpl` with a stubbed session, or an integration test, to confirm the row is written. Keep the existing v1/v2 node tests that check `process_data`.

findings.title: Pass-through __init__ added to v2 VariableAssignerNode
findings.body:
The PR adds an `__init__` to the v2 node that only forwards its four arguments to `super().__init__`. That is the default behaviour, so the method is dead weight. It also adds `TYPE_CHECKING` imports only for its signature. The v1 node also drops a parameter, so the two are now inconsistent in a different way. Removing the method keeps the diff smaller and removes a maintenance point.

::diff{file="api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v2/node.py" lines="56-68"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v2/node.py`, remove the pass-through `__init__` added around lines 56-68, since it only forwards to `super().__init__` with the same arguments. Also remove the `TYPE_CHECKING` imports if nothing else in the file uses them. Confirm `test_node_factory_creates_variable_assigner_node` still passes.

findings.title: Clean separation of persistence from node logic
findings.body: Moving the database write out of the nodes is a sound design. Nodes no longer depend on `ConversationVariableUpdater` or `ext_database`, and the `ignore_imports` exception for `variable_assigner.common.impl` is correctly removed from `.importlinter`. The layer also reads from `process_data` rather than re-deriving the update, which keeps the node output as the single source of truth. The layer filters on `NodeType.VARIABLE_ASSIGNER` and skips non-conversation selectors, so it does not touch environment variables.
